div.head: Emmanuel Old Boys v. Wilderspool Brewery.
div.p: Emmanuel Old Boys v. Wilderspool Brewery.

In Victoria Park, it being the opening match of the latter club in the Warrington and Dis- trict League Competition. Teams—Emmanuel Old Boys: T. Knight; Eccles and Harrison; Lawless, Hatton and Wainwright; Singleton, Isherwood, D. Wareham, Caldwell and Allen. . Wilderspool Brewery: Bostock ; Hunt and Daw- son; Brady, Rutter and Moores; Davenport, Oakes, D. L. Briscoe, Barnes and Livingstone. Wareham set his forwards going, and an attack on thc Brewery goal was driven back by Daw- son The game was played id a hot pace,, and the visitors' defence was kept very busy, Bos- took making several good saves. From a raid in the visitors' quarters, Allen got possession; and scored the opening goal for the Old Boys, I this being the only score before the interval. I On resuming, the visitors, ably led by Briscoe, made an onslaught on the home goal, only to and Knight very safe in his clearances. The visitors continued to attack, when Oakes tested Knight with a beauty, which was got away, but coming again the same-player was this time sue- 42re§sful in equalising the scores from a-neat pass by Barnes. From the centre kick the hoine team played in a determined manner to obtain ,the lead, but n ,they found Dawson,i spOndid "form at full-back for thovisitorst; The-game was now evenly coAtested, until Isherwood got possession and beat Bostock with a grand shot, putting his side ahead. The visitors tried hard to get on equal terms again, but could not get past the home defenders, and when time was called they had to retire defeated by two goals to one.

div.head: avenue.
div.p: avenue.
Simcock did not handle the ball during the first half.
The visitors' custodian had a different experi- ence.
lie saved his side from having double ilgures put up against them.,

The, visitors did not,relish their beating. Crosfield's splayed Orford Barracks a drawn game of three goals each at Folly-lane. Their ground has been reported by the referee as in a very unsatisfactory condition.

The workmen at -Crosfield's, who have to con- tribute to the Recreation Club, should see to it by their vote at the annual general meeting That their " Soccer " Club have a playing pitch on the Hood-lane enclosure. There is ample room to play the game there- under better conditions.
Orford St. John's beat St. Barnabas' at Long- lane and have annexed four points from them this season.
Stretford was in fine form at centre-half. Shuttleworth did not get much of a snow. Redford blade his fink appearance or St. John's.. 0

The St.,Barnabas' boys did not cause il'orbes much trouble during the afternoon. The Emmanuel Old Boys entertained Wilders- pool Brewery team at V ictoria Park. Since their team has been re-organised the Old Boys have won two and drawn one. It was no disgrace to the Brewers to be de- feated by the odd goal in three. In Mr. Briscoe they have an enthusiastic leader.
Dawson played a fine game for them at full- back.
The Brewery Lads will no doubt give a better account of themselves when they have had a little more practice. .
The Stockton Heath Reserve journeyed to Widnes minus three of their\ selected team. One of their committee completed the eleven. Glover was the best man on the field.
He is going strong for first team honours.
Broadlinrst- and V;-Toodhead, late of Latehford Recs., make their first appearance this week- end at home.
Efforts are being made to run a medal com- petition with the local League, when all junior clubs will be eligible to join.

St. George's Mission have made a smart cap- ture in IL:Roberts as goalkeeper, and T. Tully and R. Tomson. The last-named scored his initial goal with the Saints against Mill-lane on Saturday. J. W. Allen reappeared for Emmanuel Old Boys after a month's absence, and besides giv- ing a capital display on the wing he also secured the opening goal of the match. The Excelsior back—D. Wareham—was played at inside-right by the Old Boys, and, under the circumstances, he shaped creditably. The Old Boys mean to make a bold bid for the championship of the District League, their latest victims being Wilderspool Brewery. The Old Boys' Reserve were beaten on. their own ground by the Church Institute, who won by 3-1. Despite this reverse they played ex- cellent football, but the visitors were their seniors in years and altogether much. tcor, big for them, Hankinson, Rigby, Jones and Day were the pick of a good team, and these players will be tried in the League team at an early date.

Cheshire Amateur Cup on 26th December. This will prove a great game, and already excitement is running high between the supporters of both clubs over the event. div.head: CHESHIRE AMATEUR CUP. (Re-played Tie.)
div.p: CHESHIRE AMATEUR CUP. (Re-played Tie.)
Lymrn v. Latchford.

On the Lymm enclosure, to settle which should enter into the next round. Latchford introduced Bardsley and Fogg in place of well and Challinor, while the home team were at full strength. Lymm : ll'addon ; Hinde and Wilson; Clare, Woods and Daniels; Guest, Had- don, Barber, Jones and Owen. Latchford: Kite; Robinson and Bardsley; Downs, Webb and Car- ter. ; Smith, Siddall; Les, .Fogg`• and, Taylor. Latchford were the first to attack. The visitors could not get through the home half-hack line, and Bardsley had to concede several corners. Two .of these were splendidly placed ,by Clare, but no score took place, the visitors'. defer ders' playing a cool and safe game. On ene of the occasional breakaways by the visitors' forwards, the home goal was nearly captured by Lees, who brought Haddon to his knees with a grand effort. After this Latchford opened out the game more, and play was keenly and evenly contested. The interval arrived with no score being made. - The game resumed at a fast rate, and having the slope in their favour, Latchford had the best of the exchanges, Smith being very dan- gerous on the visitors' right. After a spel of attack by the home team, Latchford gradu- ally gained ground in the home territory, and from a throw-in opposite the penalty line by Downs, Lees, unmarked, got possession and scored an 4asy goal for !Latchford. Stung by this reverse, the home players buckled into their work, but met a stubborn defence in Bardsley, Robinson and Kite, they being ekinal to the occdsion. Latchford won by one goal to nil. .

div.head: NORTHWICH AND DISTRICT JUNIOR
div.p: NORTHWICH AND DISTRICT JUNIOR
COVETITION.

Stockton Heath• V. tiorthwich Rowing Club. At West Avenue, before a fair crowd of spec- tators. The home captain won the toss, and de- cided to play with the wind, and from the kick- off the Heathens got possession and quickly put the visitors' custodian on his metal. He had several good shots to deal with in the opening stages of the game. The visitors on several occasions made strenuous efforts to get into the home quarters, .but they could not get within shooting range. he Heathens had the measure of, their oplionents, and kept them on the de- fensive. Smith sent in a clinking shot, which was got away, and Antrobus received the ball jusf inside the visitors' half, beat several oppo- nents, and sent in a grand shot, which entered the top corner of the net. This was the only score made up 'to the interval. ,

On resuming the visitors showed' up to better advantage, but, Simcock cleared .easily. Good play by the home defenders transferred play to the oppoSite end, and the Rowers had a lot of work to do, and at times played a. very rough game. From a fre kick,_ which - was well placed by Gosling, Smith made a neat pass to Lockhart; to score n second goal for the Heath- ens. It was only by spasmodic rushes that the visitors ever got away from their own half Of the field. Simcock only had to handle the ball three times during the whole game, while the visit- lrs' goalkeeper saved his ,side from a double figure score. Antrobus was 'again prominent on the extreme right, a third' goal coming from one of his -centres, Jones heading into ',goal. Smith rushed up and made doubly sure .of a gcore counting. The game finished with the re-. Stockton Heath, three goals; Northwich Rowing Club, none.

verylong ere the visitors returned to the attack, and this time Roberts scored the Soldiers' second goal. After these reverses the home players opened out more in their style of play, and had more of the game, and they gradually worked their way into the visitors' lines, Mere- dith being prominent on the extreme right when he raced away nearly to the corner flag, centring finely. Munn had not much difficulty in beating Morrison. Encouraged by this suc- cess the home 'players entered into the game more keenly, and the visitors were kept more on the defence. Meredith's speed serving him well, he made a grand individual effort, which ended in making the scores equal. From now up to the interval, each end was visited in turn, but no further score took place. On turning round the game was evenly con- tested, and both defences were busy in their turn. The Soldiers showed more dash. Roberts put them in front with a shot well out of the reach of Ellison. From the centre kick the home team played hard to get on equal terms again, but they met a good defence, and not to be denied, Rowlands was successful in equalis- ing the scores. Midfield play followed, both sets of forwards being unable to break down the defence. Result: Crosfield's Reserves, three goals; Orford Barracks, three goals. .

div.head: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT LEAGUE Second Division. Orford St. John's v. St. Barnabas'.
div.p: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT LEAGUE Second Division. Orford St. John's v. St. Barnabas'.

On the 'Long-lane ground. Teams—Orford St. John's: Forbes; W. Smith and Retford; Denny, Stretford and Atherton; Tickle, 3feachin, Mill— ward, Hankinson and Sudelh St. Barnabas' : Shaw; Spruce and Long; "-Glover, Appleton and Forster; Maddock,, Woods, Shuttle Worth, Chal- linor and Brown. The opening exchanges were evenly contested, and the John's, settling into their stride, made the first ati-ack; but ware le- pulsed by Spruce.' The visitors' forwards trans- ferred play to the home quartets, and poor kicking by the home backs nearly proved fatal to them, the ball being forced over the goal line. This brought relief to the home defence, and some good passing by the home front rank was seen. Millward sent in a long shot, which-Shaw cleared in fine style. Hankinson opened the scare for the home team with a shot that Shaw never attempted to save. - Poer play by the visit- ors' half-backs let, the home forwards in. Meachin registered the second goal, and at the interval the John's' were leading by two gdals to nil. The home defenders were quickly called upon to assert themselves, and Spruce, at the 0 1 pcsite end, VIA in .some 'timely ,kicking, and Reliord showed his paces by running across and heating Woods when the latter was ,about shoot. At this juncture the visitors were having the best of matters. The homesters, however, gradually drove the visitors back, and Were awarded a free kick just outside the penalty area, which was well placed by Denny.

Widnes Institute v. Stockton Heath Reserve.

Played on the Institute ground. After the opening exchanges the visitors got near the home goal. The ball went behind. The home forwards made tracks for the visitors' goal, but could not pierce the defence. Play continued chiefly in mid-field, and when the interval arrived no score had been made.

On resuming, the visitors made an attack on the home goal and gained an unproductive cor- ner. Still keeping up the pressure, the visitors gained another corner, Richardson placing the ball well in front of the goal, but no score was made.. div.head: "THE EXAMINER" OFFICE.
div.p: "THE EXAMINER" OFFICE.
AN ELECTRIC "SPARK."
Lively Discussion in the Council Over Electricity Scheme. - . •

div.head: COUNCILLORS FALL OUT.
div.p: COUNCILLORS FALL OUT.

There were one or two lively episodes during a discussion over the extension of the electricity scheme at the meeting of the Warrington Town Council on Tuesday evening. The " spark " which led to the electrical dis- turbance came in the form of a recommendation from the Electricity Committee that the Town Clerk be instructed to apply to the Local Gov- ernment Board for their sanction to the borrow- ing of the sum of £14,550 10s. for the extension of the electricity works and plant. Dr. JOSEPH, the new chairman of the com- mittee, said the extensions were necessary to cope with the increasing demands for electricity for lighting and power purposes, for they, with their present plant, could not contend with the orders.
Councillor GOUGH : I think jve should have a full statement-from the engineer, instead of this bare, bald statement from Dr. Joseph. We should be shown what profit there would be on the outlay.
The MAYOR: On September 17th the Council had a full report from the engineer, and the Council passed it.

div.head: SCENE COMMENCED.
div.p: THE SCENE COMMENCED.

Councillor Gomm moved that the matter be referred back for a full report. The AfAiant : We have already had it. Councillor GOUGH : Unless I get further par- ticulars I stall oppose the matter before the Local Government Board inquiz. (Laughter.) Councillor Witicmsorr stron y objected to Councillor Gough making such a threat. For some time Warrington had been able to obtain borrowing powers from the Local Government Board without LIA inspector coming down to hold an inquiry. Why should the business of the Council be delayed in order to meet the fads of one or two men, who, if they had read the report of the engineer, could not retain it in their heads for a few months? The sooner such men got out of the Council the better. It was a shame for business to be frustrated in that way, when there were manu- facturers waiting to take their supplies. Councillor GOUGH : The engineer has not shown us the cost.

- Councillor WILKINSON : We better put you on all committees of the Council. (Laughter.) Power is urgently wanted by manufacturers in Warrington. Councillor Gomm: We don't know them. Councillor WILKINsox : What good would it do you if I told you? (Laughter.) Councillor GOUGH : Why should you keep that from the committee?

div.head: ,‘ INSULT TO MEMBERS."
div.p: ,‘ INSULT TO MEMBERS."

Councillor PEmBERTON : It is monstrous for Councillor Wilkinson to insult members of the Council as he does. There was not a word in this report as to the profit. We know some electricity is sold at a lower cost than it is pro- duced. How far are we to continue doing that? Councillor Wilkinson makes the wildest state- ments without the slightest responsibility. He treats the serious business of the town as if he were playing with a bowling or cricket club— but this important business, I say it's not right. (Hear, hear.) We have never had a loan with- out an inquiry—
CouneillOr WILKINSON: When we aPplied we have been granted borrowing powers without any inquiry.
eOLIRCiIII;r PEMBERTON : I say that is utterly untrue.
Councillor WILKINSON: If you stand there and say I am telling lies, what can I do with a man like you?
COULICiIIOr PEMBERTON : I believe it is ignorance on Counzillor Wilkinson's part—not a deliberate untruth.

div.head: PROFIT EVERY YEAR.
div.p: A PROFIT EVERY YEAR.

Alderman SMETHURST said the committee had made a profit every year since they took charge of the electricity concern. To-day it had £lO,OOO to its credit, with £4,000 as a working balance. The tramways stood in the same position. The new scheme had been before the Council for two years, and would have been adopted before only they delayed because they thought there were great improvements coming forward. (Hear, hear.)

Councillor PEMpERTON said they were selling electricity at a lower price than they could make it. How could they have made the money they had if the committee were doing what he suggested? They would make a great mistake if they did not pass the recommendation, as people were crying out 'for electricity. (Hear, hear.)

div.head: NOT AT A LOSS.
div.p: NOT AT A LOSS.

Councillor OSBORNE said it would be futile for anyone to suggest the spending of £14,550 for alterations and additions unless there was a de- mand for the electricity, and criticism could be lodged at the expenditure unless they could show a profit. As a matter of fact, the concern showed a lima. Councillor Pembertoi had said the electricity was supplied at less than cost, and if so there must be a good reason for It. Dr. Josses said it was quite untrue to suggest that any electricity was being sold at a loss. They tried to make an equal profit out of all their consumers. He was surprised that Coun- cillor Pemberton, as chairman of, a committee which was seeking to attract new industries to the' town, should be guilty of such a suicidal policy as not merely to reject new demands, but to run the risk of losing some of their present customers.
Councillor Gouou only found two members and himself to vote for his amendment, and was defeated by an overwhelming majority.
NURSING ASSOCIAIIW%
Annual Record of a Most Useful Work.
MORE MONEY REQUIRED.
The annual meeting of the Warrington Dis- trict Nursing Association was held on Wednes- day evening at the. Town Hall. The Mayor Presided..

div.head: DECREASED INCOME
div.p: DECREASED INCOME
In submitting the accounts for tho past year, Councillor H. Roberts, the hon. txeasurer, th his report, said •

_ It is a matter for regret that I have to report a further drop of -Xl7 13s. sd. in the income of our association, as compared with that of the previous year, and also that the total receipts have not been sufficient—apart from the balance brought forward—to meet the year's expendi- ture. It is the first time for five years that such a condition has occurred. In the last four years we have lost—principally by death or removal out of. our district-38 annual sub- scribers, representing about £4O per annum, while we have only gained 14 new subscribers, who contribute collectively about £lo—a net yearly loss of ..t3O. On the other hand our expenditure has increased and the demands for the services of, our nursing staff are greater than ever. In order to keep pace with the needs of the district it is essential that the nursing staff shall be maintained at its present strength if not increased, and in order to do this we ROW require a large number of additional sub- scribers. The greatest economy has been exer- cised by the Ladies' Committee, every member of which, under Mrs. ,Fairclough's able chair— manship, takes an active and personal interest in the Home, and their efforts are most effi- ciently supported by the Lady Superintendent (Miss Milne): whose administration is of the most capable .character. The Working Men's Committee have personally. collected a larger sum than that of the previous year, thanks to . their excellent 'organisation, and their zeal for the cause. In. order to keep our association out of debt, we require additional subscribers, to, the amount of ,t5O to £lOO per annum, and I am confident that this should not prove to be a difficult matter if the claims of the associa- tion are sympathetically considered.

div.head: INCREASED WEEKLY VISITS.
div.p: INCREASED WEEKLY VISITS.

The committee's report stated that during the year 17,280 visits were paid to 680 cases. The increase in the number of visits was 2,585- 50 additional weekly visits. There was an in- crease of 85 in the number of patients. The committee desired to express their thanks to Dr. Langdale and Dr. Fax for their professional attendances upon the nursing staff.

div.head: NURSES' EXCELLENT WORK.
div.p: NURSES' EXCELLENT WORK.

The Ladies' Committee regretted the death of Miss Massy. They also acknowledged the services of their valued Superintepdent, Miss Milne, who, in addition to her other duties, undertakes the training of candidates, of whom two have received instruction this year; the other nurses, Misses Trenham, Leech, Tweedy, Evans and Fiides, had all done most excellent work, which was highly appreciated by the patients. In consequence of the great demand for their services, anothet nurse had to be added to the staff, which added considerably to the expenditure. It was hoped that more new subscribers might be found, so that this good work would not be hampered by lack of funds. The ladies desired to thank ,all those who had sent gifts to the Home.

div.head: SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT.
div.p: SUPERINTENDENT'S REPORT.

Miss Mime, the lady superintendent, in her report, gave the following figures :—Cases transferred from last year, 49; new cases. 633; total, 680. Visits paid, 17,280, made up as fol- lows: July, 1,313; August, 1,282; September, 1,280; October, 1,535: November, 1,701; Decem- ber, 1,520; January, 1,563; February, 1,574; March, 1,887; April, 1,342; May, 1,290; June, 937. Result of cases nursed: Remaining on books, 49; convalescent, 461; transferred to hospital, 45; removed for other causes, 20; died, 115; total, 680.

div.head: NEARLY £lOO CREDIT.
div.p: NEARLY £lOO CREDIT.
The balance sheet showed that the year was commenced with a balance of £ll5 Ids. 4d. The total income was £664 9s. 9d., and the expendi- ture £.571 145., leaving a credit balance of ."..92 15s.
The Working Men's Committee report showed that £2ll 4s. 4d. had been handed to the treasurer of the Nursing Association. The total collections were £215 15s. 4d. and the expenses £4 us.

div.head: MAYOR AND WORKING MEN.
div.p: MAYOR AND WORKING MEN.

The MAYOR, proposed that the statement of accounts be adopted. He said he would become a direct subscriber. It was, he said, very satisfactory that the Working Men's Committee had collected the large sum of over ...e2OO. He thought the churches. and chapels should take up this matter more seriously than they had done, for the work of the association was of a Christian character.
Councillor G. W. JOSEPH seconded, and the report was carried.
ouncillor ROBERTS thanked the Mayor for flis kind and encouraging words, and also for his promise of practical help. The report was adopted, and the officers, &c., were re-elected en bloc.

div.head: PARIS BY NIGHT.
div.p: PARIS BY NIGHT.

You retrace your steps westtward, and look in at one of the fashionable music halls.- it seems to be' all promenade, and strikes you as very spacious, and brilliant. Men an women in search of pleasure stare at each other, hardly heeding the show, from which they are separated by rows of little private boxes, open like cattle pens. The men are mostly in evening dress—they are "creve mar- chews" or "swell" of the first water. For them the night has only begun. If your fancy so inclines you follow them. After the show you descend to the tavern or bar, beneath the hall, where the temptresses of the boule- vard have congregated. You glance at their charins, drink a glass of Lager, and follow your short-fronted swells along the Boule- vard des Capueines, you stop to see the peo- ple leaving the Opera. Across the square in frontof Garmer's magnificent building rush men in opera hats, ladies beshawled, holding their rich silks high above their dainty ankles, little girls with flowing hair. Two im- posing troopers of the Garde Republioenne, majestic and martial, sit on their chargers and direct the traffic. You jump into an "auto" :as a taxicab is called here) and are drive-li co Maxim's. You are set down before an unimposing building with red-litten win- dows, and pass through the revolving door. The fainous resort of the rich and dissipated is but a, rather haadsome restaurant where gay men and women drink champagne, and indulge in much low buffoonery till about one o'clock, when the girls often get up a dance among themselves. These res- taurants are primarily places where rsten of nominally good sound standing may shake off all restraint and behave themselves like Bank Holiday trippers. If their antics in- terest you further you may follow them at two in the morning to 'the restaurant of the Trat Mort at Montmartre where they will 'stay till dawn: then, as likely as not, driving out to' the Bois de Boulogne, to drink milk at the dairy farm, indulge in maudlin fits of remttance and resolves of amend- ment.

But these are but a small section of Pari- sians. ,No one has a greater, capacity for quiet innocent pleasure than the people o' the (ray city. If it is. a fine evening, you pass down one of the quieter streets, and see the "concierge" at No. 39 playing his etern- al game of trictrac with his neighbotir from over the road, while his wife sits and chats with the smartly beribonned "bonne" from No. 20. At the corner the young lady at "the baker's is calmly washing her poodle in the public street, while an unliterary friend stands ,by and addresses words of consolation to the suffering animal. On a Sunday night your progress down the Rue de Rivoli is apt to be interrupted by a skipping rope ex- tended across the pavement, held at one end by Monsieur Bonhomme, the grocer, and at the other by his consort, while Mimi, aged five, in ,an extremely short frock skips with frantic delight. Everywhere you realise that the whole city is the Parisian's home, where he works, eats, plays, and loves in the pub- ' eve .

ANGLING. Warrington Workingmen's Association. . N.A. CENTRE. No fish were weighed in last week, so the set prizes and specials remain as published a few weeks ago. Although fishing generally has been poor, some fine specimens have been re- corded. A list of the winners and the weights will be published next week, and if any error has occurred members who are interested should notify the secretary without delay. Not many members went out last week-end to try for the prizes of 1913 season, and those who did make journeys failed to add to the board, many members taking it for granted that the season was over for weighers. Members were trying out for rain during the season, and when we got it, what was the result? Well, as far as recording fish is concerned they failed miserably. We do not wish to say that the streams do not require • flushing now and again, but you can have too much of a good thing. THE GOWY. Take, for instance, the Gowy. After a lot of rain the stream is coffee colour. The results are always poor, but when we have the Gowy in its usual condition, or even if it is quite clear, there is always someone who has been skilful enough to bring one or two roach up to 11b. Members seem to think that the cleaning out of this stream above the mill will do considerable harm to angling. Well, for a time it may do so. but things like these will have to be done, and anglers will reap the benefit of it later on in having better banks and a better water-way, although it has disturbed their favourite spots. It will certainly have disturbed the fish from the haunts they most favoured, but, then, the angler is as likely as not to drop on the spot they have taken to. However, let us hope that things are not as bad as surmised, and wait results. AMALGAMATED GENERAL MEETING. The meeting that is to take place this year will be held in the Old Music Hall, over the Oh Post Office, in the Market Place. The date has not yet been fixed, but as there is a joint meet- ing of committees some time next week, we may be able to let members know in next week's issue. Several Northern Anglers' officials will be down, and members will be asked to bring their 'friends. More about this matter will bc. heard next week. £5. ,
